To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NLO corrections for the t¯jj process are moderate (−15%) and that the theoretical uncertainty is reduced by about a factor of two.

the NLO corrections to the production cross sections are moderate and negative, that the residual theoretical uncertainties, due to higher-order QCD corrections, amount to 21% for t¯ production at the TeVatron with a hard jet selection, and 15% at the LHC with a hard jet and a hard b-jet selection, and that the forward-backward top-quark asymmetry amounts to 4.6%, including next-to-leading order corrections.

the next-to-leading-order QCD corrections for the production of t t¯ + 2 jet final states are negative and moderate, that the residual theoretical uncertainties are 21% for TeVatron and LHC energies, and that the forward-backward top quark asymmetry amounts to 10.3 % at leading-order and 4.6 % at next-to-leading-order at TeVatron energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the NLO QCD corrections to t¯ + 2 jet production at hadron colliders.
the calculation of the cross sections for top quark pair production in the presence of additional partons in the final state, at next-to-leading-order in perturbative QCD.

the calculation of the cross sections for the production of t ¯ t in association with two additional jets at next-to-leading-order QCD, and with the study of the scale and PDF uncertainties of our NLO results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NLO QCD corrections to t¯jj production are negative and moderate, but not large enough to compensate for the large scale dependence of the leading order prediction.
the top-quark pair cross section at the TeVatron is 3.8 ± 0.6 pb and 1.0 ± 0.2 pb at the LHC, respectively.

, at the LHC, the next-to-leading-order corrections to t¯ production with two hard jets reduce the uncertainty of the theoretical predictions from 30% to 15% and increase the cross section from 0.4 to 0.5 pb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have completed the next-to-leading-order QCD calculation of the production of t t + 2 jet events, and that we have provided a detailed analysis of our NLO results.

the next-to-leading-order corrections are moderate, and the residual theoretical uncertainties are at the level of 15-21% for the integrated cross sections, and 5-7% for the differential distributions.
the calculation is now complete.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the top quark forward-backward asymmetries are not a good observable for probing new physics at the TeVatron.
the NLO corrections are large enough to warrant a more careful treatment of the scale uncertainty, which can only be done by performing an NNLO calculation.
the NLO corrections to t¯jj production at the TeVatron are large enough that the cross section for this final state is not well predicted at leading order.
